source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 20 January 1920, p. 3: "Derry Municipal Elections. North Electoral Area" (results table of all eleven counts and an account of each count). Candidates' names as nominated: Londonderry Sentinel, 6 January 1920, p. 3 ("Londonderry Municipal Nominations of Candidates").
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every count transcribed from the printed table and checked against the printed account of each transfer: every count adds to the printed valid vote of 3,220, each result is the previous result plus the transfer, and the quota is 3,220 / 12 + 1 = 269 as printed; the Unionist first preferences total 1,923 and the Nationalist 1,297, as the account says

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919; polled 15 January 1920. Counted 19 January 1920 by the returning officer, Sir Henry Miller (town clerk). The area returned 11 members; the three elected on the first count (Ballantine, R. Doherty and H. C. O'Doherty) became its aldermen. Unionist electors were advised to give preferences in ballot-paper (alphabetical) order, which is why Ballantine's surplus passed almost whole to Deane and so on down the list. Surpluses were transferred by re-examining all the elected candidate's papers and passing on the surplus in proportion; the table's non-transferable papers at counts 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 (3, 2, 1, 1, 4 and 1) were papers in those parcels with no further preference and are not part of the transferred surpluses, so they are not shown as non-transferable votes. Party labels are the Sentinel's: its "N." covers the joint Nationalist, Sinn Féin and Labour ticket and does not say which of these each candidate stood for.
